projects.name: AGI_Research
projects.description: Public lab notebook — committed daily since July 2026. Linear algebra, calculus and probability from axioms → neural nets and backprop in pure NumPy (SGD through Adam) → now CNNs, Transformers and PyTorch. No shortcuts.
projects.longDescription:
A public lab notebook committed daily since 1 July 2026 — 548 days to 31 Dec 2027. I derive everything by hand: linear algebra, calculus and probability from axioms, then neural nets, backprop, optimisers from SGD to Adam in pure NumPy, now CNNs and Transformers.

Each day is a notebook with math, code and reflection — no autograd, no shortcuts. The repo is the research log; the portfolio shows the distilled logs. Follow along as the bench grows.
highlights: Linear algebra, calculus and probability from axioms
Forward and backward pass in pure NumPy
Backpropagation derived by hand — no autograd
Optimisers from SGD to Adam, built step by step

faq.a: Daily since 1 July 2026 — the mission is 548 days to 31 Dec 2027. Each day is a notebook.

faq.q: Do you use PyTorch or pure NumPy?
faq.a: Both — I first build everything in pure NumPy by hand (backprop, Adam, CNN), then show the PyTorch version for comparison.
Yes — clone hariomlohardev/AGI_Research, open any notebook in Jupyter, and run top to bottom. No API keys needed.

projects.name: spam_classifier
projects.description: Type a message, watch it split into tokens, score red (spam) or green (ham), filter the weak signals, then stamp a verdict with P(spam|message). 5,572 messages, Naive Bayes trained in your browser — nothing mocked.
projects.longDescription:
A Naive Bayes spam filter you can see working. Type any message and it tokenises, scores each token P(spam|token) with Laplace smoothing, filters weak signals, then stamps SPAM or HAM with P(spam|message).

Trained live in your browser on 5,572 SMS messages (data.csv) via Pyodide + pandas — no mock, no server. The same Python that trained it scores you, token by token, in real time. Open the live bench and try WINNER!! free money now.
highlights: Tokenisation and scoring you can see
Weak signals filtered, strong signals kept

faq.q: Does my message leave my device?
faq.a: No — the bench runs entirely in your browser via Pyodide. Nothing is sent to a server.
Naive Bayes with Laplace smoothing (k=1) over the 5,572-row SMS dataset — the same data.csv from the repo, loaded live.
Tokens with P(spam|token) near 0.5 (weak signal, within 0.12 of 0.5) are filtered before the verdict — only strong red/green tokens count.

projects.name: practice_code
projects.description: 60+ Python solutions for algorithms and data structures, grouped by topic. Each notes time and space. Fork it, add your approach, open a PR.
projects.longDescription:
60+ Python solutions for algorithms and data structures, grouped by topic — arrays, strings, trees, graphs, DP, and more. Each solution notes time and space complexity.

Fork-friendly: add your approach in any language, keep the same folder structure, and open a PR. Built to stay readable and interview-ready.
highlights: Grouped by topic: arrays, trees, graphs, DP

faq.q: What language are the solutions in?
faq.a: Python — clean, commented, with complexity noted at the top of each file.

faq.q: Can I add solutions in other languages?
faq.a: Yes — fork, add a parallel folder for your language, keep the problem naming, and open a PR.
Yes — classic DSA patterns grouped by topic so you can drill arrays, trees, graphs or DP in order.

projects.name: pkg_jupy
projects.description: Jupyter experiments that grew up — small Python packages, utility notebooks and visualisation scratches. Open for issues and PRs.
projects.longDescription:
Jupyter experiments that grew into small Python packages — utilities, visualisation scratches and notebook helpers that I actually reuse.

Not a framework — just focused tools. Open for issues and PRs if you find a rough edge.

faq.q: What kind of packages are these?
faq.a: Small, single-purpose Python helpers extracted from notebooks — no heavy dependencies.

faq.q: Can I use them in my own notebooks?
faq.a: Yes — clone pkg_jupy, pip install -e ., and import. Issues and PRs welcome.
Not yet — they live as importable packages in the repo while they stabilise.
